title: Fractions, units and necessary conditions
topics: Denominator as unit and numerator as count of selected units
Equivalent fractions from multiplying numerator and denominator by the same positive integer
Adding unlike fractions by converting to a common unit
conditions: Fractions can be compared only when they refer to the same whole.
Multiplying numerator and denominator by the same positive integer preserves the quantity.
To add 1/2 and 1/3 of the same whole, convert both to sixths; adding denominators gives the wrong unit.
quotes: A fraction describes selected equal parts of the same whole.
Fractions must refer to the same whole before their quantities can be compared.
uncertainties: The source states the positive-integer condition for equivalent fractions but does not discuss other multipliers or define whether the multiplier may be 1.
The source gives one same-whole counterexample and one addition example, without stating further boundary cases.
